subject: physical-education
essentialQuestion: How do experienced players decide faster than they can think?

prompts.prompt: Explain the critical features or key principle of pattern recognition and anticipation in your own words.
Demonstrate or fully describe decision speed under constraint using a version your body and setting allow. A described or adapted version earns full credit.
Apply constraints-led practice design in a new situation and explain the decision or adjustment you made.
Analyze a plausible technique fault, tactical error, or unsafe choice involving scouting an opponent or a problem honestly; correct it and explain why.
Connect in-activity adjustment and its limits with coaching a tactical idea to someone else and explain how one affects the other.

Present the strongest evidence from the unit task: Design a constraints-led practice that forces a specific tactical decision, run it, and evaluate whether the decision improved — then teach the idea to one other person or write the coaching script.
Identify one thing you can now do or direct yourself, one adjustment that improved it, and one next goal you set for yourself.

adaptationChoices: Practice may be run live, walked through, simulated on paper, or modelled on a diagram; the tactical reasoning is what is assessed.
accommodationNote: Access supports may change format, pacing, intensity, range, equipment, setting, or response mode without changing the standard being assessed. An adapted or described performance is full credit, not partial credit.
neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
